title: The Fourth: Turiya
meter: Prose (the Upanishad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Mandukya Upanishad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pada and matra, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
devanagari: चतुर्थं मन्यन्ते स आत्मा स विज्ञेयः॥
translation: Not aware inward, not aware outward, not aware both ways; not a mass of awareness; not aware, not unaware. Unseen, beyond all dealings, ungraspable, without marks, unthinkable, indescribable; its essence is the certainty of the one Self; in it the world comes to rest; peaceful, auspicious, non-dual: this they consider the fourth. That is the Self. That is to be known.
translation_hi: न भीतर की ओर चेतन, न बाहर की ओर चेतन, न दोनों ओर चेतन; न प्रज्ञा का घन; न प्रज्ञ, न अप्रज्ञ। अदृश्य, व्यवहार से परे, अग्राह्य, लक्षणरहित, अचिंत्य, अवर्णनीय, एक आत्मा के अनुभव का सार, जहाँ संसार शांत हो जाता है, शांत, शिव और अद्वैत: इसे चतुर्थ (तुरीय) माना जाता है। वही आत्मा है, वही जानने योग्य है।

words.note: As in the Argala Stotram verse 8.

words.meaning: whose essence is the certainty of the one Self
where the world comes to rest

words.note: a + dvaita (duality). The name of Shankara's school.

grammar: The way of negation: eight a- words in a row (अदृष्ट, अव्यवहार्य, अग्राह्य…). Turiya can only be pointed at by saying what it is not, exactly as Nirvana Shatkam does.
Gerundives -ya: ग्राह्य, चिन्त्य, व्यपदेश्य, विज्ञेय 'to be grasped, thought, described, known'. With a-, 'not to be…'.
Shivam advaitam: 'auspicious, non-dual'. Here shiva is an adjective; the refrain of Nirvana Shatkam, शिवोऽहम्, draws on this mantra.
